story_type: teen adrift alone on a kayak at night, infrared search, boat pickup
hook: She drifted for hours in the dark, with no paddle.
narration: A seventeen year old girl drifted alone on a kayak in the Gulf of Mexico, in the dark, with no paddle.
She had been kayaking with her family off Tarpon Springs, Florida.
Then a passing boat's wake hit her kayak, and she lost her paddle.
She drifted away from her family for hours, into the evening.
At six that night, after her family reported her missing, the Coast Guard launched a search by air and by sea.
This is an infrared camera. It sees heat, so a person glows white against the cooler water, even in total darkness.
[short pause] At six minutes past ten, a helicopter crew spotted her.
The helicopter stayed overhead and guided a twenty nine foot boat from Station Sand Key straight to her.
The boat crew reached her and pulled her aboard.
outcome: The crew recovered her in stable condition after a four hour search and took her back to her waiting family.
title: 17-year-old adrift at night, no paddle
description:
On April 10, 2016, a Coast Guard helicopter crew found a 17-year-old girl drifting on a kayak off Tarpon Springs, Florida, after a four-hour search, and a boat crew from Station Sand Key pulled her aboard.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Chief Petty Officer David Schuhlein, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/458363/coast-guard-rescues-17-year-old-girl-after-4-hour-search-gulf-mexico
